title: Multi-SDK credential compactor + ergonomic stream facade (py/ts/go) and parity test suite
author: Aisha Morgan
release_notes: Adds a lightweight credential compactor and ergonomic streaming facade across Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs; improves auth/retry parity and adds conformance tests. No public API breaking changes; minor version bumps planned for each SDK.
description: Context: teams saw subtle mismatch in behavior when a pipeline of token refresh, heartbeat, and stream resume interacted under high churn. Motivation: reduce auth noise, provide a single compact credential lifecycle primitive ("CredentialCompactor") that coalesces refresh calls, exposes a stable lease window, and surfaces a minimal ergonomic streaming facade that standardizes resume vs restart semantics across SDKs. What this PR does: 1) Introduces CredentialCompactor implementations in sdks/python, sdks/typescript, and sdks/go. The compactor centralizes TTL jitter, backoff damping, and a single-flight refresh that prevents refresh storms; it also exposes metrics hooks for telemetry. 2) Adds an ergonomic StreamFacade which unifies async generator/async iterator behavior (Python/TS) and the pull-based iterator for Go, with explicit resume tokens and idempotent retry semantics. 3) Harmonizes retry presets: we standardized the SDK retry weights and hedged/latency-aware defaults so cross-language behavior is consistent under the same linear test scenarios. 4) Adds 3 new end-to-end parity test suites (py/ts/go) that exercise credential handoff during stream preemption, token rotation under heavy churn, and resume semantics after transient network partitions. 5) Small doc updates and examples demonstrating migrating from per-call refreshers to the compactor primitive. Design notes: the compactor is not a session store; it is lightweight, in-process, and intentionally exposes a small surface: acquire_lease(), refresh_hint(), and close(). It uses a soft lease window (lease_expiry - jitter) and singleflight semantics to ensure no concurrent outbound refreshes for the same logical credential key. StreamFacade provides two high-level behaviors: resume_if_token_present (resumes with KV cursor) and restart_clean (explicit restart that drops cached prefixes). This PR keeps the legacy lower-level hooks for backwards compatibility but marks a small set of helpers as deprecated with migration notes. Tests & CI: unit tests added for all languages, cross-sdk conformance harness validates identical traces for three canonical scenarios, and the e2e matrix ran on GHA against a mocked control plane. CI summary: unit: pass; lint: pass (TS required minor typemap fix); typecheck: pass; integration: pass after one flaky test was retried and stabilized; e2e: pass. Migration plan: ship as minor releases for sdks (Python 1.13.0, TS 1.27.0, Go 1.8.0) and mark legacy helpers deprecated but not removed. Rollout: feature flagged on server side for a small percentage initially, with telemetry counters to detect increased refresh latency or unexpected rejection rates. Backward compatibility: compat shim keeps previous per-call refresh working; most customers can opt-in to compactor by replacing the token provider with the compactor wrapper. Security: compactor integrates with existing KMS/HSM token unwrap code paths; no new secrets are persisted. Implementation highlights: Python: sdks/python/redwood/auth/compactor.py (CredentialCompactor class), sdks/python/redwood/stream/facade.py (async generator wrapper), tests: tests/e2e/parity/test_compactor_parity.py. TypeScript: sdks/typescript/src/auth/compactor.ts (compactLease, singleFlightRefresher), sdks/typescript/src/stream/facade.ts (AsyncGeneratorFacade), tests: tests/integration/compactor-parity.spec.ts. Go: sdks/go/auth/compactor.go (Compactor), sdks/go/stream/facade.go (PullIterator facade), tests: internal/e2e/compactor_parity_test.go. Commits: see commits list below. Files changed: see changed_files list below. Review conversation summary: initial review flagged two things: (a) TS type export leakage where an internal symbol was accidentally exported; (b) potential deadlock in Go compactor when Close() races with an in-flight refresh. Both were addressed: TS fix narrowed exports and added an extra type alias for the public surface; Go fix added cancelation propagation and a small lock ordering rework. Final reviewers approved. Merge: squash and merge after green CI. Why this is different from previous auth/retry work: instead of only synchronizing retry presets or token handoff, this PR consolidates the lifecycle orchestration pattern (coalescing refresh) into an intentionally small primitive and pairs it with a standard stream consumer facade across languages, improving developer ergonomics and making parity tests less brittle. Known limitations: compactor is in-process and therefore does not handle multi-process credential caching (future follow-up will add a sidecar/shared cache pattern); resume behavior assumes models that support cursor resume semantics; some older examples using per-call refreshers might require small adapter code. Related: ENG-3421 (investigate refresh storms), ENG-3490 (parity test plan). Merge method: squash and merge.
